$comment: The BitCent (B¢) frozen issuance record. scripts/deploy-qct-bitcoin.js loads THIS file -- it never hardcodes tokenomics. A Rune's name, divisibility, cap and premine are immutable at etch, so this record is the single place those values may be set, and 'ratified: false' on any field is a hard refusal to broadcast, not a warning. See codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/2026-07-30_bitcent-frozen-issuance-record.md for the original history and codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/2026-07-30_bitcent-governed-reserve-ratification.md for the 2026-07-30 governed-reserve amendment that ratified the three fields below. codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/2026-07-29_qriptocent-supply-constitution.md is the ten-item freeze list this implements.

divisibility.note: Operator ruling 2026-07-30: 2, not 18 -- B¢ is already a cent-denominated unit; 0.01 B¢ = one ten-thousandth of the reference dollar. Supersedes the 8 previously coded here and the 18 raised for discussion.

maxSupply.note: Ratified 2026-07-29, qriptocent-supply-constitution.md. Independent of Base Q¢'s own 1,000,000,000 -- per-denomination, not per-chain.

premine.note: AMENDED 2026-07-30 (governed-reserve model, operator ruling). Supersedes the 2026-07-29 ratification of 100,000,000, which conflated the ON-CHAIN premine (the single custodial output the Rune protocol actually etches) with the INITIALLY-ACTIVE operational amount. The full 1,000,000,000 B¢ -- the entire maxSupply -- is premined in one output to the ratified premineCustodian address; nothing further can ever be minted (openMint: none, see mintTerms below). Only 100,000,000 of that premine is authorised for initial operational use; the remaining 900,000,000 sits in the SAME custodial output under a governance constraint (see mintTerms.governedReserve) rather than a separate on-chain split -- Bitcoin Runes has no protocol-level mechanism to partition a premine into 'active' vs 'reserved' tranches at the UTXO level. The record must be candid about that: this is a 1B on-chain premine with a 100M/900M GOVERNANCE distinction, not a 100M on-chain premine.

mintTerms.note: RATIFIED 2026-07-30 (governed-reserve model, operator ruling). Supersedes the pre-consolidation code's unratified amountPerMint=1000/cap=900000000 placeholder, which implied a permissionless PUBLIC open mint -- explicitly rejected ('Do not open a permissionless public mint'). openMint: 'none' means the Etching carries NO Terms structure at all: no public minting transaction of any kind can ever add supply after the etch. initiallyActiveIssuance (100,000,000) is the amount the allocationSchedule below distributes and Aigent Nakamoto's treasury-cap check enforces for pilot spend authorisation; governedReserve (900,000,000) cannot be released from the premineCustodian address without a NEW operator mandate and a governed treasury action -- this is a spend-authorisation policy enforced by the pilot treasury authority gate (services/treasury/pilotTreasuryAuthority.js), not a protocol-level lock. divisibility is NOT duplicated here -- it has its own ratified top-level field above; one authoritative location per concern.

allocationSchedule.note: RATIFIED 2026-07-30 (operator ruling). Sums to 100,000,000 -- the initiallyActiveIssuance tranche (mintTerms.value.initiallyActiveIssuance), NOT the full 1,000,000,000 on-chain premine. These are TREASURY EARMARKS: an internal allocation of purpose against the active tranche. They do NOT independently authorise any transfer -- every actual movement still requires the full pilot treasury authority chain (operator mandate + passcode + Aigent Z execution + Aigent Nakamoto approval + Aigent Kn0w1 observation).

premineCustodian.note: RATIFIED 2026-07-30 (operator ruling) -- pilot custody model: 'Aigent Z BitCent Treasury'. A fresh testnet keypair generated for this role (never reused from any prior exposed key). Aigent Z is the operational treasury custodian -- not MoneyPenny (orchestrates the Financial Services Runtime but must not control the issuance reserve), not Aigent Nakamoto (oversees Bitcoin issuance integrity/governance with approval-or-veto authority over issuance-sensitive acts, but does not hold custody). PILOT-AUTHORISED -- PROVISIONAL SECURITY PROFILE: this is a SINGLE-KEY testnet wallet, not the threshold/multisig control this field originally required before ratifying -- the operator explicitly accepted this trade-off for pilot speed, substituting the pilot treasury authority gate's multi-party chain (operator mandate + passcode + Aigent Z execution + Aigent Nakamoto approval + Aigent Kn0w1 observation) for on-chain multisig. See codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/2026-07-30_pilot-treasury-authority.md for the full gate and codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/2026-07-30_bitcent-governed-reserve-ratification.md's post-pilot review trigger (signer topology, Platform Aletheon participation, passkey replacement, key rotation, custody separation) for what supersedes this before any non-pilot use. The private key (BITCENT_TREASURY_CUSTODIAN_WIF) is held by the operator server-side only -- never committed, never logged.

relationshipToBaseQc.value: independent native ledgers; cent-for-cent protocol settlement via DVN-mediated debit-and-credit; no wrapped-token bridging; no lock-and-mint

independenceDeclaration.value: BitCent (B¢) and Base Q¢ are separate canonical denominations of one stable-value class (QriptoCENT), each with its own native ledger and independently governed maximum supply. Neither is a wrapped or bridged representation of the other.

etchBroadcast.$comment: OBSERVATIONAL, appended 2026-08-02 — a record of what HAPPENED, not a frozen issuance parameter. Nothing above this key is altered. It exists because the record had no way to say the etch had been broadcast, so every downstream reader had to treat an already-etched name as an open question — and scripts/check-bitcent-name-availability.js answered "LIKELY AVAILABLE" about a name we ourselves had already etched, which is the one direction that could cause a second, irreversible etch.

verification.$comment: OBSERVATIONAL RECEIPT, appended 2026-08-02 — the result of decoding the etch transaction's own OP_RETURN with the same runelib encoder that built it (scripts/verify-bitcent-etch.js). This is PRIMARY evidence: it depends on no indexer. It settles the question the 404 could not — the Runestone is well-formed, so the transaction is a valid etch and NOT a cenotaph. Nothing above this key is altered; no ratified issuance parameter is touched.
verification.verifiedBy: operator, on their own machine (npm run verify:bitcent-etch)
verification.method: scripts/verify-bitcent-etch.js — Runestone.decipher over the raw transaction hex
verification.indexerDisagreement: mempool.space's testnet Rune endpoint returns 404 for BITCENT and has done so through 16,038 confirmations. That is an INDEXER limitation, not a protocol failure: it does not answer Rune queries on testnet. The etch record, not the indexer, is authoritative for this name.
verification.consequence: The etch does not need to be repeated. The original governed act stands. Mainnet issuance remains a separate ratification with its own record — this testnet etch does not authorise it.
